reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the role of configurational entropy in stabilizing solid solutions but also cautions that ordering enthalpy can overcome entropy at low temperatures, and it does not address diffusion suppression or nanoparticle stability at high temperatures. E2 discusses catalytic performance and electronic effects, not structural stability or diffusion. Thus, the key premises on lattice distortion suppressing diffusion and preventing segregation up to ~1800 K lack specific prior evidence.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered solid solution against segregation at high temperatures.
Severe lattice distortion in HEAs suppresses atomic diffusion.
Suppressed diffusion prevents elemental segregation and phase separation up to ~1800 K.
Stability is maintained under inert atmospheres within the catalytic/thermoelectric range (473–1923 K).
Segregation onset is expected only above a critical temperature (~1800 K) or after prolonged exposure.
